question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: Ensemble suggests a high likelihood (0.90) of recording at least 1,000 Mediterranean deaths by end-April 2026 given an early-year pace of ~606 deaths by Feb 23.
Objections argue the pace may not sustain into March–April, and that enhanced SAR capacity, safer corridors, or deterrence policies could reduce crossings and fatalities.
Data reporting gaps and revisions add uncertainty about near-term tallies, though the threshold remains plausible if March–April conditions support continued elevated fatalities.
Calibrated probability: moderate (centered around 0.70) with a range of 0.60–0.80, reflecting credible near-term risks without ruling out hitting 1,000.

justification.critique_assessment: The objections are valid and highlight credible near-term risks (pace sustainability, SAR/policy shifts, and data gaps) that could plausibly dampen the chance of hitting 1,000 by May.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from the ensemble 0.90 to a calibrated 0.70 with a 0.60–0.80 range to reflect credible risks identified in the objections.

causal-factors.name: Pace of early-2026 Mediterranean fatalities
causal-factors.rationale: IOM data through February 23, 2026 show about 606 deaths/missing on the Mediterranean, signaling an unusually high start to the year that substantially increases the chances of crossing 1,000 deaths by end-April.

causal-factors.name: Historical annual toll baseline (approx. 2,000–2,500 per year on the Mediterranean)
causal-factors.rationale: With a historically high annual toll, sustaining the early-year pace into March–April makes reaching 1,000 deaths by May plausible.

causal-factors.name: Weather/sea conditions in March–April 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Storms and rough seas can drive more shipwrecks, raising fatalities and pushing the count toward 1,000 by May.

causal-factors.name: Policy crackdown on irregular migration in Europe
causal-factors.rationale: Tighter controls and deterrence measures could reduce crossings, potentially limiting fatalities despite high early-year risk.

causal-factors.name: Data reporting gaps and revision risk
causal-factors.rationale: Missing Migrants data are subject to lag and revision, adding uncertainty to whether the end-April total will reach 1,000.

causal-factors.name: Weather and sea-state conditions in March–April 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Storms and rough seas raise the risk of capsizes and drownings, potentially driving fatalities higher if dangerous crossings persist.

causal-factors.name: Sustained high crossing flows from Libya/Tunisia
causal-factors.rationale: Continued migration pressure and many departures increase the number of boats at risk, elevating total deaths through April.

causal-factors.name: Search-and-rescue capacity and policy environment
causal-factors.rationale: Stronger rescue operations and safer corridors can reduce fatalities, reducing the odds of hitting 1,000 by May.

causal-factors.name: Data reporting lags and under-counting by MMP
causal-factors.rationale: Unreported or late-reported incidents could lift the final tally beyond what is currently visible.

causal-factors.name: Single high-casualty incidents (e.g., Crete capsizes)
causal-factors.rationale: Major accidents can produce outsized monthly death totals, nudging the cumulative total upward.

synthesis: The high ensemble probability is tempered by credible near-term risks to sustaining the pace and by data/reporting uncertainties. A calibrated estimate around 70% (range 60–80%) best reflects the balance between plausible continuation of the early-year toll and plausible reductions due to SAR/policy changes or reporting gaps.
